2.translation: ## Nested source regions retain their own namespaces ⟦shared:0⟧

3.translation: A detail may itself be a Fusion. This example uses two explicit windows on the unchanged pUC19 source. The inner source is the larger window; its child is the smaller window. The outer selection targets the inner source through ⟦shared:0⟧, not an arbitrary rectangle in an image.

6.translation: ⟦shared:0⟧ plus ⟦shared:1⟧ connects derived regions/fronts/leaders to each original selection in ⟦shared:2⟧. Top-level ⟦shared:3⟧ remains the original outer input. Nested leaf names use paths such as ⟦shared:4⟧ and ⟦shared:5⟧; a composition container is never treated as one genomic axis. If an accession occurs in multiple leaves, select the full panel path and exact instance. ⟦shared:6⟧ can select a source leaf under ⟦shared:7⟧. Layout exports include actual mm boundaries and requested boxes/angles.

7.translation: Each plot keeps its own layers, scales and statistical population; the compositor does not silently copy layers or recompute statistics. Origin wraps use the explicit source-length declaration below. The complete negative-strand CDS-to-genome-focus-to-real-character example is in ⟦shared:0⟧. Registered characters retain their physical tile/error policy; a small nested allocation cannot make 60 letters readable merely by increasing DPI. Full multi-device publication acceptance and broader layout optimisation remain separate concerns.

9.translation:
Circular layout is not evidence of a circular source. Set ⟦shared:1⟧ on a
selection with ⟦shared:0⟧. Both selected leaf panels must retain the same
full source length. Character adapters additionally require ⟦shared:2⟧
and ⟦shared:3⟧ with a full sequence or an exact ⟦shared:4⟧; without the
full string, characters remain unverified. At most one source tour is allowed,
so inverse source-to-column mapping stays unique. Negative strands wrap in
their own direction and retain gaps. Different focused instances are never
joined implicitly.

10.translation:
Run the complete real pUC19 workflow in ⟦shared:0⟧. It extracts
82 observed bases (2640–2686, then 1–35) from the unchanged bundled FASTA.
⟦shared:1⟧ retains the original single row. Derived tables identify
two pieces with ⟦shared:2⟧, sharing one ⟦shared:3⟧; only the two external
boundaries receive leaders. The seam is not another selection or relationship.
